$comment: Human Repair Graph — the two vocabularies every capability is classified by. Both come from the owner's founding draft (owner-draft-2026-07-26.md): the five pillars became the five grid columns in v0.2; the action primitives are her 'useful hierarchy'. Neither list is open-ended: adding a member is an explicit, logged decision.

classes.name: Sense
classes.question: Can we measure the state of this target in a living person?

classes.name: Model
classes.question: Do we know what a healthy target state for it is, and can we predict the effect of an intervention?

classes.name: Reach
classes.question: Can we deliver something to it, specifically and repeatedly?

classes.name: Edit
classes.question: Can we repair, replace, reprogram, regenerate or clear it?

classes.name: Verify
classes.question: Can we confirm afterwards that it worked, and stayed working?

classes.name: Control
classes.question: Can we time, dose, localise and stop the intervention safely while it runs?
classes.note: Added in v0.3 for the survival-phase capabilities (haemostasis, perfusion, stabilisation) that are neither an edit nor a measurement. The only class added since v0.2; logged here.

primitives.name: Stop what is destroying
primitives.definition: Halt a catastrophic process before it destroys something that cannot be recovered: bleeding, hypoxia, arrhythmia, shock, seizure, toxin, uncontained infection.

primitives.name: Remove what should not be there
primitives.definition: Pathogens, toxins, cancer cells, senescent cells, scar tissue, misfolded aggregates.

primitives.name: Repair what can be repaired
primitives.definition: DNA, mitochondria, proteins, membranes, epigenetic state — in place, in the existing cell.

primitives.name: Regenerate what is missing
primitives.definition: Limbs, nerves, cartilage, muscle, vasculature, appendages — new structure with correct architecture.

primitives.name: Reconnect what must communicate
primitives.definition: Neural circuits, immune regulation, endocrine loops, vascular continuity.

primitives.name: Recalibrate control loops
primitives.definition: Immune, endocrine and metabolic signalling set-points.

primitives.name: Preserve what defines the person
primitives.definition: Memories, identity, learned abilities, preferences, agency, consent. Not an appendix: a system requirement every other primitive is constrained by.

boundary.statement: Repair is possible when the relevant information still exists, can be inferred, or has been backed up.
boundary.consequence: Nodes whose target state cannot be inferred from surviving information (destroyed identity-bearing neural structure without a backup) are marked informationLimited: true and are never graded above L0 for 'restore the original', only for 'reconstruct a new one'.

gradeLadder.$comment: Unchanged from v0.1 (records/rubrics.json). Anchored on observables; independent replication is the anchor a lab cannot award itself.

blockedKinds.definition: We do not know how. The binding constraint is knowledge or capability.
We know how, and it is not reaching people: approvals, ethics, economics, access, manufacturing.
Not blocked at the current rung; the next rung is a matter of running the demonstration.
